title.zh: 卷一百〇七 表第二: 宗室世系表
title.raw: 卷一百〇七 表第二: 宗室世系表 Volume 107 Tables 2: Imperial Clan Genealogy

sentences.zh: 自昔帝王之興，莫不眾建子弟，以蕃王室，所以崇本支、隆國勢也。

translations.literal: From antiquity when emperors arose, none failed to establish many sons and younger kinsmen to buttress the royal house — this is how the root branch is honored and national strength elevated.
translations.idiomatic: Since antiquity, whenever emperors have risen to power, they have invariably enfeoffed many sons and younger kinsmen to strengthen the royal house — honoring the root line and magnifying the state's power.

sentences.zh: 觀其屬籍有圖，玉牒有紀，大統小宗，秩乎不紊，蓋亦慎矣。

translations.literal: When one views their registry charts and jade genealogical records, the major lines and minor branches are ordered without confusion — truly meticulous.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by their clan registers and jade genealogical rolls, major lines and minor branches are kept in proper order without confusion — a matter of real care.

sentences.zh: 然以唐室之盛，自玄宗後，諸王不出閤而史已失其世次，況後世乎？

translations.literal: Yet for all the Tang house's greatness, after Emperor Xuanzong the princes did not leave their pavilions and the histories already lost their generational sequence — how much more so in later ages?
translations.idiomatic: Yet even at the height of the Tang, after Emperor Xuanzong the princes never left their quarters and the histories had already lost track of their generations — to say nothing of later dynasties?

sentences.zh: 元之宗系，藏之金匱石室者甚祕，外廷莫能知也。

translations.literal: The Yuan clan genealogy, stored in golden caskets and stone chambers, was extremely secret; the outer court could not know it.
translations.idiomatic: The Yuan imperial clan genealogy was kept in golden caskets and stone vaults with the utmost secrecy, so that the outer court could not know it.

sentences.zh: 其在史官，固特其概，而考諸簡牘，又未必盡得其詳，則因其所可知，而闕其所不知，亦史氏法也。

translations.literal: In the historical offices they give only the outline; examined against documents one may not obtain every detail — then to record what is known and omit what is unknown is also the historians' method.
translations.idiomatic: The historical offices can give only the broad outline, and even when one consults the documents one may not recover every detail. To set down what is known and leave blank what is not is likewise the historians' way.

translations.literal: Composes the Imperial Clan Genealogy Table.
translations.idiomatic: Here is composed the Imperial Clan Genealogy Table.

sentences.zh: 太宗皇帝，七子：長定宗皇帝，次二闊端太子，次三闊出太子，次四哈剌察兒王，次五合失大王，次六合丹大王，次七滅里大王。

translations.literal: Taizong Emperor, seven sons: eldest Dingzong Emperor, second Kuoduan Crown Prince, third Kuochu Crown Prince, fourth Harqachar Prince, fifth Heshi Great Prince, sixth Heden Great Prince, seventh Mieli Great Prince.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizong Emperor had seven sons: the eldest was the Dingzong Emperor; second, Kuoduan, Crown Prince; third, Kuochu, Crown Prince; fourth, Prince Harqachar; fifth, Great Prince Heshi; sixth, Great Prince Heden; seventh, Great Prince Mieli.

sentences.zh: :按憲宗紀有云：太宗以子月良不材，故不立為嗣。

translations.literal: Note: According to the Annals of Shizong it states that Taizong, finding his son Yue Liang incompetent, therefore did not establish him as successor.
translations.idiomatic: Note: According to Shizong's annals, Taizong considered his son Yue Liang incompetent and therefore did not establish him as successor.

sentences.zh: 今考經世大典帝系篇及歲賜錄，並不見月良名字次序，故不敢列之世表，謹著于此，以俟知者。

translations.literal: Now examining the Imperial Lineage section of the Comprehensive Institutions of Governance and the Annual Stipend Register, neither shows Yue Liang's name or sequence; therefore I dare not list him in the lineage table — I record him here with care, to await those who know.
translations.idiomatic: On examining the imperial-lineage section of the Comprehensive Institutions of Governance and the Annual Stipend Register, I find neither Yue Liang's name nor his proper sequence; I therefore dare not enter him in the lineage table and record him here instead, until someone better informed may clarify.

translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong had three sons. The eldest, Crown Prince Aratnadara, died young and left no descendants;

translations.idiomatic: the second was Crown Prince Yantughus and the third Crown Prince Taipingne; both likewise died young without issue.

translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ningzong died in youth and left no sons.

sentences.zh: 順皇帝，三子：長皇太子愛猷識理達臘，餘二子，蚤世。

translations.literal: Emperor Shun had three sons: the eldest was Crown Prince Ayushiridara; the other two died young.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shun had three sons. The eldest was Crown Prince Ayushiridara; the other two died in youth.

sentences.zh: 按十祖世系錄云：始祖孛端叉兒收統急里忽魯人氏民戶時，嘗得一懷姙婦人曰插只來，納之，其所生遺腹兒，因其母名曰插只來，自後別為一種，亦號達靼。

translations.literal: According to the Record of the Ten Ancestors' Genealogy: when the ancestor-founder Boduanchid received the households of the Tümenilqur people, he once obtained a pregnant woman named Cha'ijilai and took her in. The posthumous child she bore, because of his mother, was named Cha'ijilai; thereafter they formed a separate branch, also called Tatar.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of the Ten Ancestors' Genealogy states that when the founding ancestor Boduanchid took in the households of the Tümenilqur people, he once received a pregnant woman named Cha'ijilai. He took her in, and the posthumous son she bore was named after his mother, Cha'ijilai. From that time they formed a separate line, also known as the Tatars.

sentences.zh: 今以非始祖親子，故不列之世表，附著于此云。

translations.literal: Now because he was not a son of the ancestor-founder by blood, he is not entered in the genealogy table but is appended here.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was not a son of the founding ancestor by blood, he is not listed in the main genealogy table but is recorded here as an appendix.
